notes.hashRouting: jitsi-meet routes rooms by path (/RoomName). The production server answers any non-asset path with the app shell, so path routing survives a root-mounted proxy. It does not survive being mounted under a sub-path.
notes.startup: npm run preview:build runs the install and build stages; npm run preview:start runs the start stage (npm start -> server/index.js), which binds the port from PORT (no flags) and refuses to start if the build output is missing. Both stages do less than a release build, because a preview runner has fewer minutes and less memory. The install stage runs npm install with MEETSPACE_SKIP_MOBILE=1, so postinstall applies the patches/ overrides and skips the three React Native steps (jetify, android-clean-cmake-cache, android-autolinking); patch-package is never skipped, since the bundles are compiled from the patched sources. The build stage runs npm run build:preview (make preview), not npm run build: it sets MEETSPACE_PREVIEW=1, which builds 6 of the 9 bundles with no source maps (alwaysontop, documentpip and close3 are absent from build/ and libs/), and it sizes the V8 old-space heap to this machine (75% of total memory, capped at 8192 MB, floored at 2048 MB) instead of asking for a fixed 8 GB. Every bundle the served page pulls is built, so the app that starts is the whole app. Demo mode (node demo/start.js, npm run demo) is a separate development path and is not what the preview runs.
notes.externalDependencies: None to build, start or browse. Signalling is only contacted once a room is actually joined, at the backend named by MEETSPACE_BACKEND.
notes.failureClassification: Both preview commands go through scripts/preview.js. When a stage fails it prints exactly one line of the form "[preview] STAGE=install|build|start STATUS=failed", followed by the command, the exit status (a kill reads as exit=137 signal=SIGKILL, which is what running out of memory during the build looks like) and the last lines of that stage output. Grep the preview log for "[preview] STAGE=" to tell dependency installation, compilation and application startup apart. Stage output itself is streamed through unchanged.
